item.title: Math Tricks
item.description: Distance between rotations If you want the distance between two rotations you could compute the relative rotation like this: $$R = R_1^T * R_2$$Then you can extract the axis and angle. Usually this is done with quaternions. $$q = q_1^* q_2$$Where \(^*\) is the conjugate. The length of the vector part is: $$a = \sqrt{ q_v \cdot q_v }$$Then you can get the angle: $$\theta = 2 * \operatorname{atan2}(a, q_s)$$But this required an expensive square root and arctangent.

item.title: How to Transform a Plane
item.description: Suppose you have a plane equation in local space and you’d like to express that plane equation in world space. The plane in local space is written as: $$P := (n, w)$$where \(n\) is the plane normal and \(w\) is the plane offset. A point \(x\) is on the plane if $$n \cdot x = w$$Now define a transform \(A\) as $$A := (R, p)$$where \(R\) is an orthonormal rotation matrix and \(p\) is a translation vector.
